input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The separator selection negates any_prefix_is_slash, picking ' / ' exactly when an option spelling already starts with a slash and '; ' otherwise.
- failure path: An option declared as --shout/--no-shout renders in --help as '--shout; --no-shout', and a Windows-style /debug;/no-debug option renders as '/debug / /no-debug', where the slash separator is indistinguishable from the slash prefix of the names.

Reviewer finding
- description: The separator condition is reversed, changing existing help output for options with secondary spellings.
- rationale: For a boolean option declared as `--foo/--no-foo`, `any_prefix_is_slash` is false, so the new method displays `--foo; --no-foo` instead of `--foo / --no-foo`. Options using slash prefixes likewise receive ` / ` where the previous implementation used `; `, regressing the help formatting during extraction.
critique: The finding names the same inverted separator condition on any_prefix_is_slash. Its failure cases also match the label: `--foo/--no-foo` renders with `; `, and slash-prefixed options get ` / `.
